items.metric: LIVE GMV (in-progress week Sep 14 to 20 vs Sep 7 to 13, third week of decline)
items.effect: 96 streams in the in-progress week produced 307.62, or 3.20 per stream against 17.02 in the completed week, so live is a yield problem rather than a scheduling one.
items.action: Re-brief boldvideos7, holder of the top four streams at 515.00, 371.75, 355.03 and 310.80, and hold stream volume near 116 instead of adding it.

items.effect: Affiliate share of GMV fell to 61.8% from 86.7%, so the creator channel is shrinking faster than the shop total.
items.action: Move sample approvals into shipment today, since affiliate GMV follows sample delivery by one to two weeks.

items.metric: GMV (in-progress week Sep 14 to 20, six complete days, vs Sep 7 to 13; third week of decline; 10 metrics in three week runs)
items.effect: Day normalized the week runs at 508.09 against 1,030.93, so the -57.8% is partly the missing seventh day and the attribution lag after Sep 13.
items.action: Track the Sep 20 close, which needs 4,167.97 in one day to reach parity, and keep approvals and shipping moving as the only input lever that reaches October GMV.

items.metric: Sample requests (third week of decline, upstream of affiliate content)
items.effect: Fewer inbound requests plus a 53.7% rejection rate starves the sample to video to GMV chain in late September and October.
items.action: Clear the 36 To Review requests today, highest post rate first, before the 13 that expire today and the 17 that expire by Sep 22 lapse.

items.metric: Sub-1.0 GMV Max campaigns blended ROAS against breakeven 1.0 (Shop Wide 0.781, Back to School 0.679)
items.effect: The pair spent 704.17 for 516.11 of revenue in the completed week, about -188.06 of contribution before COGS and commission.
items.action: Move that 704.17 of spend into Screen Door at 1.95 and Bidet 7/6 at 1.989, the two campaigns that clear breakeven.

items.effect: 161 of 300 requests are still refused, so more than half of inbound sample demand never reaches a shipment.
items.action: Screen on post rate and gpm before rejecting, since 12 of the 35 rated pending requests sit at 90% post rate or better.
